article_title: Investing in a High-Quality Teacher Workforce: Lessons from Texas Teacher Preparation Programs
citation: Bland, J. A., Ralph, K., Wei, W., Wang, V., Wojcikiewicz, S. K., & Wechsler, M. E. (2025). Investing in a high-quality teacher workforce: Lessons from Texas teacher preparation programs. Learning Policy Institute. https://doi.org/10.54300/871.327
title: High-quality preparation pattern: practice-based coursework tightly coupled to a full-year, gradual-release clinical experience with trained mentor co-teachers
description: The three profiled programs share a design in which scaffolded, rigorous coursework is linked to "a full year of intensive, gradual-release clinical practice under the guidance of an experienced mentor teacher". Candidates experience the complete school year as co-teachers, take on responsibilities from day one, and follow delineated timelines for progression of responsibilities and co-teaching practices. Assessments shifted from evaluating what candidates know to what they can do, and course content is sequenced to add complexity progressively across preclinical and clinical years.
requirements: Purposefully selected and trained mentor teachers who co-teach, monitor candidates' progression, and provide feedback and coaching
Structures delineating general timelines for candidates' progression of responsibilities throughout the school year
constraints: The report notes some structures are still being enhanced as implemented, and each case study emphasizes different program components to varying degrees
target_learners: Undergraduate and postbaccalaureate teacher candidates at minority-serving institutions
target_learning_goals: Day-one readiness to lead a classroom
Integration of coursework content with clinical teaching practice
examples: UH expanded student teaching from one semester to two and made the yearlong residency the standard for all undergraduate candidates (about 300 per year); UTRGV additionally offers a yearlong clinical experience called STEP UP
key_sources: Bland, J. A., Ralph, K., Wei, W., Wang, V., Wojcikiewicz, S. K., & Wechsler, M. E. (2025). Investing in a high-quality teacher workforce: Lessons from Texas teacher preparation programs. Learning Policy Institute. https://doi.org/10.54300/871.327

article_title: From disengaged to self-determined: a latent transition analysis of students' AI learning motivation
citation: Liang, S., Yau, K. W., Meng, H., Chiu, T. K. F., King, I., Yam, Y., & Chai, C. S. (2026). From disengaged to self-determined: A latent transition analysis of students' AI learning motivation. Education and Information Technologies. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10639-026-13998-y
title: Year-long school-based AI curriculum with hands-on activities and AI-enabled chatbots
description: A 12-chapter school-based AI curriculum developed by Chiu et al. (2022) covering machine learning, computer vision, speech and language processing, ethical and societal implications, and the future of work. The article reports that "The curriculum incorporated hands-on activities, case-based discussions, and interactive learning tasks supported by AI-enabled chatbots, allowing students to explore how AI systems operate and how they influence everyday decision-making." Participating teachers attended a professional development workshop on the curriculum's pedagogical design before implementation.
requirements: Teachers attended a professional development workshop familiarizing them with the curriculum structure, learning objectives, and teaching resources before implementation
constraints: The article notes curriculum fidelity and exact instructional methods were not systematically observed across schools, which may have introduced variability in students' experiences
target_learners: Secondary school students in Grades 7 to 9
examples: Implemented across 53 Hong Kong secondary schools over one academic year, with learning activities connecting AI concepts to real-world applications
key_sources: Liang, S., Yau, K. W., Meng, H., Chiu, T. K. F., King, I., Yam, Y., & Chai, C. S. (2026). From disengaged to self-determined: A latent transition analysis of students' AI learning motivation. Education and Information Technologies. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10639-026-13998-y

article_title: A cognitive-ecological approach to preventing aggression in urban settings: Initial outcomes for high-risk children.
citation: Metropolitan Area Child Study Research Group. (2002). A Cognitive–Ecological Approach to Preventing Aggression in Urban Settings: Initial Outcomes for High-Risk Children. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037//0022-006X.70.1.179
title: Yes I Can social–cognitive classroom curriculum
description: Yes I Can is a 40-lesson social–cognitive classroom curriculum delivered to all children in the classroom over 2 years as the core of the Level A general enhancement intervention. It "covered five areas of social cognition, each related to risk for aggression: self-understanding/self-efficacy, social perspective taking, normative beliefs about aggression, social problem-solving skills, and behavioral scripts." Lessons were linked to reading and math, and teachers were trained via biweekly seminars with fidelity monitoring.
requirements: Delivery with teacher consultation focused on classroom management, prosocial behavior, and cultural competency; trained teacher collaborators and fidelity monitoring
constraints: In this trial the classroom-only condition showed no significant aggression or detectable effects for high-risk children when delivered early or late
target_learners: All children in elementary classrooms regardless of risk, in low-income urban schools
target_learning_goals: Social cognition skills related to aggression risk: self-efficacy, perspective taking, normative beliefs, problem-solving, and behavioral scripts
examples: Teachers received 2 years of biweekly seminars; 94% demonstrated mastery of content at or above the 80% level, and teachers were observed at least four times per academic year
key_sources: Metropolitan Area Child Study Research Group. (2002). A Cognitive–Ecological Approach to Preventing Aggression in Urban Settings: Initial Outcomes for High-Risk Children. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-006x.70.1.179

article_title: Supporting online learners’ regulation skills with the help of learning analytics and generative artificial intelligence
citation: Mutluhan Yilmaz, Andrea Gauthier, Mutlu Cukurova. (2026). Supporting online learners' regulation skills with the help of learning analytics and generative artificial intelligence. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10595-1
title: Ye and Pennisi's framework for modelling SRL from LMS behavioural traces
description: The study adopts Ye and Pennisi's (2022) theory-based framework that integrates Pintrich's SRL model (forethought, planning, activation, monitoring, control, reflection) with the Online Self-Regulated Learning Questionnaire as a lens for collecting and modelling LMS log data. The authors chose it because "the SRL skills indicators it provides are aligned with behavioural traces that can be captured from online learning platforms", enabling assessment across all SRL cycle phases. It maps SRL phases to LMS behavioural data and OSLQ indicators, and the study operationalised it into five proxies: goal setting, task strategies, time management, help-seeking, and self-evaluation.
requirements: Course resources must closely correspond to the framework's indicators so data sources align conceptually and practically with the measurement model
constraints: The study's course lacked Optional Self-Assessments and bonus quiz completion indicators, so these two were excluded from proxy computation
examples: Raw MOODLE log events were extracted, normalised and z-score standardised, then aggregated into the five SRL proxies used for clustering and feedback generation
key_sources: Mutluhan Yilmaz, Andrea Gauthier, Mutlu Cukurova. (2026). Supporting online learners' regulation skills with the help of learning analytics and generative artificial intelligence. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10595-1

article_title: Improv and Ink: Increasing Individual Writing Fluency with Collaborative Improv
citation: DeMichele, M. (2015). Improv and ink: Increasing individual writing fluency with collaborative improv. International Journal of Education & the Arts, 16(10). http://www.ijea.org/v16n10/
title: Internalization of 'Yes, and...' as an inner-speech writing prompt explains improv's effect on writing fluency
description: The article theorizes that students internalize the improv rule "Yes, and..." through repeated collaborative practice, consistent with Vygotsky's (1978) account of inner speech in which external self-talk is gradually internalized. Students first say "Yes, and..." aloud in oral games, then think it before each offer in narrative games, and finally apply it as an internalized prompt during collaborative and individual writing. The author presents this as the mechanism by which improv helps students add consecutive thoughts and increase writing length.
requirements: Repeated practice of "Yes, and..." across a progression of oral, collaborative written, and individual writing activities
constraints: The author presents this as an interpretation of descriptive data rather than a directly tested mechanism
target_learners: Adolescent high school writers, including reluctant writers
target_learning_goals: Develop writing fluency by connecting thoughts into complete sentences
key_sources: DeMichele, M. (2015). Improv and ink: Increasing individual writing fluency with collaborative improv. International Journal of Education & the Arts, 16(10). http://www.ijea.org/v16n10/

article_title: Improv and Ink: Increasing Individual Writing Fluency with Collaborative Improv
citation: DeMichele, M. (2015). Improv and ink: Increasing individual writing fluency with collaborative improv. International Journal of Education & the Arts, 16(10). http://www.ijea.org/v16n10/
title: Frame collaborative creative work with the rule 'Yes, and...' to build trust, reduce self-criticism, and support reluctant learners
description: The article argues that improv's foundational rule "Yes, and..." — accepting another player's offer and building upon it — distinguishes improv from other improvisational activities and creates a collaborative, non-judgmental frame. Through consistent practice students learn to suspend judgment of themselves and others, building trust, confidence and self-esteem. The author suggests this social-emotional foundation helps reluctant writers reengage and develop the confidence needed to put their own thoughts on paper.
requirements: Consistent practice of accepting and building on others' offers within structured games
constraints: The article distinguishes improv from improvisational activities like role-playing that lack the "Yes, and..." frame
target_learning_goals: Build confidence and willingness to express ideas in writing
key_sources: DeMichele, M. (2015). Improv and ink: Increasing individual writing fluency with collaborative improv. International Journal of Education & the Arts, 16(10). http://www.ijea.org/v16n10/

article_title: The Effectiveness of a Simulation-Based Menopause Education Program.
citation: Collazo Madison MD, Meade Aaliyah, Marko Emily MD, Slater Amanda, Hu Inchi PhD, Davis Carolyn MD. (2026). The Effectiveness of a Simulation-Based Menopause Education Program. MedEdPORTAL. https://doi.org/10.15766/mep_2374-8265.11625
title: Repeat simulation training yearly rather than offering a single session
description: The article states that "repeated training is likely more beneficial" than completing one simulation session, and reports that the authors' OB/GYN residency program has implemented the session into its didactics curriculum so residents can practice these skills yearly. The recommendation rests on the authors' stated hope rather than on a tested comparison of single versus repeated sessions.
requirements: Integration of the session into a residency didactics curriculum
constraints: The benefit of repetition is asserted, not tested, in this article
target_learners: OB/GYN residents and residents of adopting institutions
target_learning_goals: Maintaining and improving knowledge and confidence in managing menopausal needs
examples: The authors' program implemented the session into the residents' didactics curriculum allowing yearly practice
key_sources: Collazo Madison MD, Meade Aaliyah, Marko Emily MD, Slater Amanda, Hu Inchi PhD, Davis Carolyn MD. (2026). The Effectiveness of a Simulation-Based Menopause Education Program. MedEdPORTAL. https://doi.org/10.15766/mep_2374-8265.11625
